exams.syllabus: ABRSM Bowed Strings Practical Grades from 2024. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Pieces 30 each (90 total, 60%); Scales and arpeggios 21 (14%); Sight-reading 21 (14%); Aural tests 18 (12%); total 150. Pass 100–119, Merit 120–129, Distinction 130–150 (Below Pass 50–99). A pass in every component is not required to pass overall.

Three pieces, one from each of Lists A (faster, technical agility), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied traditions/styles); at least one must be accompanied. Live piano (or listed string) accompaniment required except for pieces marked SOLO; Initial–Grade 3 may use string accompaniment/duets (DUET or DUET/PIANO; candidate plays the upper part unless stated). Candidates bring their own accompanist (teacher may accompany; no recorded accompaniment; accompanist may simplify). Listed editions are mandatory only for arrangements/transcriptions. Da capo and dal segno must be observed; other repeats (incl. first-time bars) omitted unless very short. Cadenzas omitted unless specified; long tuttis cut; either ossia allowed. Memory optional, no extra marks. Teacher/accompanist may tune at Initial–Grade 5; candidates tune themselves at Grades 6–8. Scales, sight-reading and aural unchanged from the previous syllabus.
sections: Scales & technical work
Scales: D, A majors from open strings, 1 oct., separate bows, even notes or long tonic (candidate's choice); E minor from bottom E to a 5th, separate bows, even notes. (All three played.)
Sight-reading

4 bars (4/4) or 6 bars (2/4); time: 4/4 or 2/4; new features: 1st position; crotchet and quaver note values, crotchet rests; notes separately bowed; mf; new keys: D, A majors; range: d′–g′, a′–d″. Unaccompanied; 30 seconds to prepare; parameters are cumulative from earlier grades.
Aural & other tests
Clap the pulse; clap back rhythm echoes of two 2-bar phrases; sing back two 1-bar echoes (tonic–mediant, major); answer a question on dynamics or articulation of a piece.
Performance Grades / digital option

Performance Grades (Initial/Grade 1–8) use the same repertoire lists but consist of four pieces (three from the lists plus one own choice) and a mark for the performance as a whole, with no scales, sight-reading or aural; currently assessed by video-recorded submission. The same Grade 5 prerequisite applies for Grades 6–8 and marks cannot be transferred between the two.

comps: Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). Viola: G6-8 one piece may be on violin from the Violin list. Double bass: max one all-pizzicato piece. Harp: Initial-G3 pieces playable on pedal or lever harp unless marked. Pieces published with accompaniment must be accompanied (single instrument, piano unless approved). Face-to-face: recorded accompaniment/backing track allowed up to Grade 3, live accompaniment from Grade 4; page turner allowed G6-8. Vibrato expected from Grade 5 (bowed). Repeats of 4 bars or fewer observed, longer repeats omitted unless stated; D.C./D.S. observed; cadenzas only if stated; memory optional (no extra marks). Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100, no technical work or supporting tests. Same grade boundaries as face-to-face. Backing tracks/recorded accompaniment allowed at all grades in digital exams.

exams.syllabus: Trinity Strings syllabus (from 2025). Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). Viola: G6-8 one piece may be on violin from the Violin list. Double bass: max one all-pizzicato piece. Harp: Initial-G3 pieces playable on pedal or lever harp unless marked. Pieces published with accompaniment must be accompanied (single instrument, piano unless approved). Face-to-face: recorded accompaniment/backing track allowed up to Grade 3, live accompaniment from Grade 4; page turner allowed G6-8. Vibrato expected from Grade 5 (bowed). Repeats of 4 bars or fewer observed, longer repeats omitted unless stated; D.C./D.S. observed; cadenzas only if stated; memory optional (no extra marks). Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100, no technical work or supporting tests. Same grade boundaries as face-to-face. Backing tracks/recorded accompaniment allowed at all grades in digital exams.
sections: Technical work

1) Bowing: candidate picks a G8 scale/arpeggio; examiner picks one of the G5-7 bowings (martelé, spiccato, hooked). EITHER 2) tonal centres G, A, Bb, Db/C#, Eb 3 oct (scales separate or three octaves to a bow, one bow up/one down; arpeggios separate or slurred nine); chromatic from Bb, C, D 2 oct (separate or slurred twelve); diminished 7ths from A#, C, D 2 oct (separate or slurred eight). Min: scales and arpeggios dotted crotchet 88, 7ths crotchet 92. Technical exercises (crotchet = 88): Bb major thirds 2 oct, G major sixths 2 oct, D major octaves 1 oct. OR 3) Orchestral extracts (music allowed): prepare three (Orchestral Violinist bk 2), play two: tone - Mendelssohn Sym. 4 III or Wagner Meistersinger Overture; bowing - Brahms Sym. 4 IV or Prokofiev Romeo & Juliet (Masks); left hand - Glinka Russlan Overture or Mussorgsky/Ravel Pictures (Tuileries).
Supporting tests

Sight reading (compulsory) + aural OR improvisation. Sight reading (30s prep, about two grades below the exam; cumulative): adds 2/2 and changing time signatures; duplets; double stops with two stopped notes (not in sequences); keys all major and minor keys. Aural: 12-16-bar harmonised major or minor piece in 2, 3, 4, 6 or 5 time - time signature, dynamics, articulation (one hearing); three other characteristics; with a copy, locate three changes as pitch or rhythm. Improvisation: stylistic - 16 bars over piano (impressionistic or irregular dance, 5 time, adds C#/F minor, all chords incl. 7ths, 9ths, suspensions); motivic - 12-16-bar unaccompanied response to a 1-bar motif; harmonic - unaccompanied over a chord sequence (8 bars x2; all chords, 7ths, 9ths, suspensions; keys C, D, E, F, G, A, Bb major; A, B, C#, D, E, F#, G minor).

exams.name: ARSM
exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for violin, read from the ABRSM PDF (55 entries). Refer to www.abrsm.org/programme-arsm for programming requirements. List valid from 2017 until further notice. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ATCL repertoire list for violin, read from the Trinity PDF (41 entries). Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified. Programmes may use list pieces, own-choice pieces or both, but any own-choice repertoire must be pre-approved. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.

Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. sections: About the repertoire list

Official LTCL repertoire list for violin, read from the Trinity PDF (33 entries). Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified. Programmes may use list pieces, own-choice pieces or both, but any own-choice repertoire must be pre-approved. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required. Learning outcomes add contextual understanding and the candidate's own musical voice.

p0005.d: An energetic contemporary piece for violin and piano by Eleanor Alberga; the title suggests soaring, adventurous writing with rhythmic drive and wide-ranging virtuosity.
p0005.rw: Fresh, exciting modern showpiece; hard to source

p0008.d: Kreisler's elegant violin version of Albéniz's best-known Tango: a lilting, slightly melancholy dance tune with sweet double-stops and plenty of room for stylish rubato.

p0009.d: Opening movement of Alwyn's Sonatina for violin and piano: a graceful, lightly neoclassical Allegro in an English idiom, more about poise and clean shaping than display.

p0018.d: A short unaccompanied caprice by Bacewicz, herself a virtuoso violinist: idiomatic, energetic writing with chords and rapid figuration in a modern idiom.

p0019.d: Bacewicz's unaccompanied Polish Caprice: a brilliant, folk-flavoured miniature built on Polish dance rhythms, with chords, rapid passagework and a strong rhythmic drive.
p0019.rw: Brilliant solo showpiece; great for confident players

p0020.d: A short violin and piano piece by Bacewicz whose title, 'Stained-glass window', suggests a colourful, image-based miniature with vivid modern harmony.

p0024.d: The energetic finale of Bach's C minor sonata for violin and keyboard: a vigorous fugal Allegro where violin and harpsichord trade lines on equal terms.

p0025.d: The finale of Bach's E major concerto: a lively rondo with a dancing refrain alternating with increasingly brilliant solo episodes.
p0025.rw: Bright and cheerful; shows clean technique

p0026.d: The Allemanda from Bach's D minor partita: flowing, continuous lines in a dignified dance, with implied harmony and subtle shaping in an unaccompanied texture.
p0026.rw: Great Bach; exposes intonation and phrasing

p0028.d: Any of Bach's six sonatas for violin and obbligato harpsichord: mostly four movements alternating expressive slow movements with fugal fast ones, in true duo partnership.

p0029.d: Any complete Bach sonata or partita for solo violin: a cornerstone of the repertoire, combining fugues, dances and slow movements with polyphonic chord writing.
p0029.rw: Summit of violin repertoire; huge payoff

p0032.d: Opening movement of Bach's E major concerto: a radiant movement built on the three-note rising motif, with a minor-key middle section and da capo return.
p0032.rw: Joyful Bach; good balance of skills

p0033.d: The complete E major concerto: a joyful first movement, a profound C-sharp minor Adagio over a repeating bass, and a dancing rondo finale.

p0036.d: The Tempo di Borea (Bourrée) and its Double from Bach's B minor partita: a bold, chordal dance followed by a running variation in continuous quavers.

p0037.d: The famous sparkling Preludio from the E major partita paired with the stately Loure: perpetual-motion brilliance followed by a slow, graceful dance.

p0038.d: The noble, chordal Sarabanda and the racing Giga from Bach's D minor partita: a pairing contrasting deep expressiveness with brilliant passagework.

p0039.d: The elegant Loure and cheerful Gavotte en Rondeau from Bach's E major partita: graceful dance music with gentle chords and a catchy rondo tune.

p0044.d: The gentle, chordal Siciliana and the fiery perpetual-motion Presto from Bach's G minor solo sonata.

p0046.d: The singing Andante, with its melody over a steady pulsing bass played on one violin, and the energetic Allegro finale of the A minor solo sonata.

p0048.d: The serene Largo and brilliant Allegro assai from Bach's C major solo sonata: a calm, singing movement followed by a fast, bright finale of running semiquavers.

p0081.d: Barber's complete violin concerto: two richly lyrical, romantic movements followed by a short, ferociously fast perpetual-motion finale.

p0082.d: Opening movement of Barber's violin concerto: a long, warm, singing melody in a romantic style, with expansive phrasing and climaxes rather than flashy display.
p0082.rw: Gorgeous melody; rewards a big tone

p0084.d: Three short dances from Bartók's Romanian Folk Dances in Székely's violin version: a lamenting horn melody, a stamping dance and a quick, lively finale.

p0086.d: Bartók's early two-movement concerto, a musical portrait of Stefi Geyer: a rapturous, slowly unfolding first movement and a playful, capricious second.

p0087.d: Bartók's complete second violin concerto: three movements of sweeping lyricism, folk-based rhythm and virtuoso writing, with the finale transforming the opening material.

p0089.d: Bartók's first rhapsody (violin or cello version): a slow, swaggering lassú followed by a fast, increasingly wild friss built on folk dances.

p0091.d: Bartók's unaccompanied sonata, written for Menuhin: a Bach-inspired Chaconne-tempo opening, a formidable fugue, a hushed Melodia and a scurrying Presto.

p0094.d: Bax's first violin sonata: a large, richly romantic work with lush, rhapsodic writing and Celtic colour, revised several times.

p0096.d: A warm, broadly lyrical romance with a passionate climax, written for the violinist Maud Powell; asks for sustained tone and expressive shaping.
p0096.rw: Gorgeous melody; great vehicle for tone

p0097.d: Opening Allegro of Beach's large-scale late-Romantic sonata: sweeping, Brahmsian and stormy, with a rich piano part and demanding ensemble.
p0097.rw: Big, passionate Romantic sonata; rewarding partnership

p0102.d: Sparkling rondo finale of the G major sonata: bright, perpetual-motion fiddle writing with rustic drone-like episodes and wit.
p0102.rw: Brilliant, cheerful finale; needs clean fast fingers

p0105.d: A serene, song-like rondo, originally for violin and orchestra (piano reduction), with gently decorated returns of the main theme; tests tone and poise.
p0105.rw: Beautiful melody; tests tone and control

p0106.d: Calm, hymn-like romance opening with double stops; alternates the main theme with contrasting episodes, demanding a pure sustained tone.
p0106.rw: Lovely and dignified; double-stop opening exposed

p0107.d: Cheerful 6/8 rondo finale of Beethoven's first violin sonata, full of bouncing rhythms and witty dialogue with the piano.
p0107.rw: Joyful, well-paced finale; good ensemble showcase

p0109.d: Beethoven's monumental 'Kreutzer' Sonata: fierce, concerto-like outer movements and a variation slow movement; huge stamina and power needed.
p0109.rw: Towering, thrilling; very long and demanding

p0110.d: Beethoven's monumental 'Kreutzer' Sonata: fierce, concerto-like outer movements and a variation slow movement; huge stamina and power needed.

p0111.d: Restless, driving presto in 6/8 from the A minor sonata, terse and urgent with close interplay between violin and piano.

p0114.d: Light-hearted, playful opening Allegro vivace of Op.12 No.2, with skittish exchanges between violin and piano.
p0114.rw: Witty and neat; less weighty than others

p0115.d: Gentle, flowing opening Allegro of the A major Op.30 sonata; understated and lyrical, needing refinement over display.
p0115.rw: Refined music; less showy for exams

p0117.d: Complete Op.12 No.2: a skittish, humorous Allegro vivace, a plaintive A minor Andante and a graceful, flowing finale.
p0117.rw: Witty, charming; less dramatic than others

p0118.d: Dramatic, tightly argued opening of the C minor sonata, with brooding tension, sudden outbursts and martial rhythms.
p0118.rw: Gripping drama; a favourite with examiners

p0120.d: Complete Op.12 No.1: confident, bright opening, a set of variations, and a bouncing 6/8 rondo finale; Classical clarity throughout.
p0120.rw: Sunny, well-balanced sonata; ideal diploma choice

p0122.d: The famous 'Spring' Sonata complete: sunny, lyrical first movement, a serene Adagio, a tiny tricky scherzo and a genial rondo.

p0123.d: Opening of the 'Spring' Sonata: one of Beethoven's most beloved singing melodies, with flowing dialogue and gentle energy.

p0124.d: Two movements from Beethoven's last violin sonata: intimate, pastoral and subtle rather than showy, with a hymn-like slow movement and variation finale.

p0125.d: Bright, bustling opening of the G major sonata, full of running figures and humour; quick, light and athletic.
p0125.rw: Sparkling and fun; needs clean agility

p0126.d: Complete G major Op.96: gentle trill-based opening, a hymn-like Adagio, a bucolic scherzo and a variation finale; intimate and subtle.
p0126.rw: Sublime late sonata; subtlety over display

p0135.d: A movement from Berg's twelve-tone 'To the memory of an angel' concerto: haunting and emotionally intense, quoting a Carinthian folk tune and a Bach chorale.
p0135.rw: Masterpiece; deeply moving and very demanding

p0136.d: Berg's complete concerto, a requiem for Manon Gropius: lyrical, haunting and complex, with a searing climax and serene Bach chorale ending.

p0140.d: Unaccompanied work pairing a searching, rhapsodic introduction with a vigorous, contrapuntal Allegro; neoclassical in style and harmonically tart.

p0147.d: The great unaccompanied passacaglia closing Biber's Rosary Sonatas: variations over a repeated four-note descending bass, contemplative and searching.
p0147.rw: Profound Baroque solo; needs stylistic insight

p0152.d: The impassioned, improvisatory centrepiece of Baal Shem: cantor-like modal melody, fiery climaxes and free rubato; a big emotional statement.

p0153.d: The impassioned, improvisatory centrepiece of Baal Shem: cantor-like modal melody, fiery climaxes and free rubato; a big emotional statement.

p0157.d: Joyful finale of Baal Shem, celebrating the Rejoicing of the Law: lively folk-dance rhythms, double stops and festive energy.
p0157.rw: Exuberant, festive; good contrast to Nigun

p0196.d: The stormy finale of Brahms's D minor sonata: driving 6/8 rhythms, heavy chords and urgent passagework set against a rich piano part. Exciting but needs power and control of sound.
p0196.rw: Thrilling finale; real chamber music partnership

p0197.d: The warm, gently flowing opening movement of Brahms's sunniest violin sonata, full of song-like melodies and close partnership with the piano. Needs a long line and tonal warmth more than fireworks.
p0197.rw: Glorious lyrical music; ideal for a warm tone

p0198.d: Brahms's most relaxed and lyrical violin sonata: an amiable opening Allegro, a slow movement alternating with a lively dance, and a heartfelt finale. Subtle rather than flashy; tests phrasing and ensemble.
p0198.rw: Glorious, lyrical sonata; teacher and audience favourite

p0199.d: Two movements from Brahms's most dramatic violin sonata, which ranges from a restless opening Allegro and a hymn-like Adagio to a quicksilver scherzo and a stormy Presto finale.
p0199.rw: Intense, powerful sonata with superb variety

p0200.d: Brahms's most dramatic violin sonata in four movements: restless opening Allegro, hymn-like Adagio, quicksilver scherzo and a stormy Presto agitato finale. Demands power, sustained tone and close partnership.
p0200.rw: Intense, powerful sonata with superb variety

p0209.d: The gentle, expansive opening movement of Brahms's first violin sonata, built from a quiet dotted-rhythm motif into passionate climaxes. Subtle and intimate; needs tonal warmth and flexible phrasing.

p0210.d: Brahms's autumnal first violin sonata ('Regen'): a gentle, expansive Vivace, a deeply felt Adagio and a finale that quotes his Regenlied. Intimate rather than showy; needs warmth and close ensemble.
p0210.rw: Glowing, intimate sonata; a chamber-music treasure

p0213.d: A short, breathless perpetual-motion piece for violin and piano, with continuous fast notes demanding even fingers, clean string crossings and stamina. Light, witty and brilliant.
p0213.rw: Brilliant encore piece; short for an ARSM programme

p0217.d: A concert study for violin and piano based on a bugle call: fanfare-like figures, rapid flourishes and brilliant double stops. Quirky and technically demanding but short.
p0217.rw: Witty showpiece; demanding for its brevity

p0222.d: Britten's early suite for violin and piano: a sharp March, a whirling Moto perpetuo, a Lullaby, and a closing Waltz, introduced by a motto. Witty, edgy and technically brilliant.

p0224.d: The impassioned first movement (Vorspiel) of Bruch's concerto: improvisatory recitatives, a soaring main theme and a short link straight into the slow movement. Rewards a big, warm sound.
p0224.rw: Hugely popular; big tone pays off

p0225.d: The vigorous, Hungarian-flavoured finale of Bruch's concerto: a double-stopped dance theme, a broad lyrical second subject and an accelerating Presto coda. Thrilling and brilliant.

p0226.d: Bruch's beloved concerto in full: an improvisatory prelude, a deeply lyrical Adagio, and a brilliant double-stopping finale. Rich, warm and immediately appealing.

p0228.d: A slow, singing Romance for violin and orchestra, broad and melancholy, with expressive climaxes. Calm in character; tests sustained tone more than virtuosity.
p0228.rw: Lovely but low-key for a fellowship

p0229.d: Bruch's four-movement fantasy on Scottish folk songs, ending with a vigorous 'Scots wha hae' finale. Lyrical, picturesque and full of double stops and virtuoso writing.

p0248.d: A tender, song-like romance for violin and piano with a flowing melody and gentle salon-style charm. Needs warm tone and expressive shaping.

p0251.d: Chausson's single-movement Poème for violin and orchestra: dark, brooding and rhapsodic, rising to intense climaxes with double-stopped passages. A haunting fin-de-siècle mood piece.

p0271.d: A lively dance from Coleridge-Taylor's Four African Dances for violin and piano, with rhythmic vitality, folk-inspired melody and warm harmony. Short and characterful.

p0272.d: Coleridge-Taylor's lyrical violin concerto, written for Maud Powell: a broad, songful first movement, a tender slow movement and a lively finale. Warm and Romantic.

p0276.d: Three movements from Corelli's F major sonata: a lively Vivace, an expressive Adagio with optional ornamentation and a bright, dancing Allegro. Classic Baroque violin writing.

p0284.d: The lively closing Allegro from a French Baroque violin sonata: bright, dancing music with running passages and crisp bowing.

p0289.d: Debussy's compact late three-movement sonata: fantastical, fleeting, with free rhythm, pizzicato colour and Spanish touches. Demands extreme colour and rhythmic flexibility.
p0289.rw: Cello masterpiece; compact, colourful, impresses examiners

p0291.d: Debussy's last completed work: three compact, quicksilver movements moving from veiled melancholy to whimsical fantasy and a brilliant finale. Needs colour, rhythmic flexibility and ensemble finesse.
p0291.rw: Masterpiece; short yet rich, superb with pianist

p0293.d: A lush, rhapsodic single movement in Delius's richly chromatic style, with long singing lines rising to an impassioned climax. Needs warm tone and sustained phrasing more than flashy technique.
p0293.rw: Lovely tone piece; less known, less showy

p0298.d: Delius's late violin sonata, dictated to Eric Fenby: three short movements, pastoral and wistful, with a lilting dance-like middle movement. Needs sweet tone and flexible phrasing.
p0298.rw: Beautiful, intimate; less virtuosic than rivals

p0299.d: The finale of Delius's last violin sonata: a lyrical, flowing movement with nostalgic warmth and folk-like touches, ending quietly. Calls for refined tone and phrasing.
p0299.rw: Charming but low-key for a diploma

p0313.d: A lively salon mazurka with snappy dotted rhythms, characterful accents and a sweeter middle section. Calls for rhythmic flair and charm in a violin-encore style.
p0313.rw: Charming encore piece; light but effective

p0317.d: A big-hearted first movement in Bohemian Romantic style, unusually leading straight into the slow movement. Lyrical themes alternate with demanding passagework and double stops.
p0317.rw: Warm, idiomatic; less hackneyed than rivals

p0318.d: Dvořák's warmly lyrical violin concerto: a rhapsodic first movement flowing into a song-like Adagio, then a sparkling furiant-flavoured rondo finale full of folk dance energy.

p0323.d: A tender, flowing single-movement romance with a long-breathed melody over a gently pulsing accompaniment, rising to warm climaxes. A test of sustained tone and phrasing.

p0327.d: The broad, warm opening movement of Dvořák's F major sonata, with flowing lyrical themes and rich interplay with the piano. More about tone and ensemble than display.

p0330.d: A quirky, playful salon piece from Elgar's early violin pieces: skittish rhythms, sudden accents and humorous character changes. Short and witty.

p0332.d: A vast, emotionally complex first movement with noble themes, intricate passagework and dense double stops. Among the most demanding Romantic concerto movements.
p0332.rw: Magnificent but exceptionally long and hard

p0333.d: Elgar's epic concerto: a noble, complex first movement or the vast finale with its famous accompanied cadenza. Huge technical and interpretive demands.
p0333.rw: Magnificent but exceptionally long and hard

p0337.d: The sonata's mysterious, intimate Romance and its broad, lyrical finale, which recalls earlier themes. Needs warm tone, nuance and sustained expressive arc.
p0337.rw: Rich, mature music; lovely tone showcase

p0338.d: An energetic, passionate first movement with surging arpeggios, double stops and a lyrical second theme. Dense textures demand strong tone and stamina.

p0339.d: Elgar's only violin sonata: a vigorous first movement, a mysterious Romance and a broad, lyrical finale. Rich, autumnal music demanding tone and stamina.
p0339.rw: Rich, mature music; lovely tone showcase

p0344.d: An unaccompanied violin piece named after the monsoon (Varsha), likely drawing on Esmail's Hindustani-influenced style with ornamented, flowing lines. Details inferred.

p0345.d: Kreisler's arrangement of the dance from Falla's opera: fiery Spanish rhythms, flamenco colour, and brilliant double stops and harmonics. A crowd-pleasing encore.

p0348.d: Kochański's arrangement of the mysterious, sensuous Pantomime from El amor brujo: a slow, sultry melody over shifting rhythms. Needs rich tone and atmosphere.

p0350.d: Kochański's violin arrangement of Falla's Seven Spanish Popular Songs: vivid miniatures from the lilting El paño moruno and hushed Nana to the fiery Polo.
p0350.rw: Colourful and varied; loved by audiences

p0358.d: The passionate, surging first movement of Fauré's A major sonata, with sweeping lines over a rippling piano part. Needs ensemble sense, tone and rhythmic flow.

p0359.d: Fauré's youthful, passionate sonata: surging first movement, tender Andante, delicate scherzo and lyrical finale. Fresh, melodic and closely partnered with the piano.

p0366.d: Either of two Finzi slow pieces for violin and orchestra/piano: quiet, pastoral, deeply English music with long-breathed melody and restrained intensity.

p0367.d: The jaunty finale of Finzi's early violin concerto: a bright hornpipe-style rondo with energetic dotted rhythms and English folk flavour, lighter than his pastoral style.

p0373.d: The impassioned Recitativo-Fantasia and the radiant canonic finale of Franck's sonata: wide expressive range, from improvisatory brooding to glowing lyricism.

p0374.d: The dreamy, lilting opening Allegretto and the turbulent, virtuosic second movement Allegro, with its stormy piano part. Demands stamina and ensemble power.

p0376.d: Franck's great cyclic sonata: dreamy opening, turbulent Allegro, improvisatory Recitativo-Fantasia and radiant canonic finale. A summit of the violin-piano repertoire.

p0381.d: Françaix's early sonatine: four brief, witty movements full of Parisian charm, crisp rhythms and quirky harmony. Light-hearted but needing precise, agile playing.

p0402.d: Glazunov's lush, single-span Romantic concerto: soaring melody, a tricky cadenza and a hunting-horn finale with double stops and spiccato.
p0402.rw: Glorious melodies; major showpiece for its length

p0412.d: A violin arrangement of Granados's Aragonese jota: bright, strummed dance energy framing a lyrical, folk-like song.
p0412.rw: Colourful Spanish piece; fun to play

p0414.d: Opening movement of a contemporary Maltese violin sonata, based on Maltese dance (Żifna): rhythmically lively with folk colour.

p0415.d: The middle movement of Grieg's third violin sonata: a tender, folk-like romance with a livelier dance-like central section.

p0416.d: The middle movement of Grieg's G major sonata: a gentle, folk-tinged melody framing a lively Norwegian dance episode.

p0417.d: Grieg's sunny G major sonata, full of Norwegian folk-dance rhythms and melody; fresh, youthful and dramatic by turns. The set movements are the folk-tinged Allegretto and the energetic dancing finale.

p0420.d: Grieg's sunny G major sonata, full of Norwegian folk-dance rhythms and melody; fresh, youthful and dramatic by turns.

p0421.d: Grieg's most dramatic violin sonata: stormy and passionate outer movements around a tender, songlike Romanze. Needs a big tone and strong rhythmic drive.

p0422.d: The first movement of Grieg's C minor sonata: stormy, passionate and dramatic, with a tender lyrical second theme.
p0422.rw: Thrilling drama; very satisfying to play

p0425.d: A short, lyrical contemporary piece for violin and piano by Scottish composer Helen Grime; delicate, expressive lines in a modern harmonic language.
p0425.rw: Modern lyrical choice for expressive players

p0426.d: A short, lyrical contemporary piece for violin and piano by Scottish composer Helen Grime; delicate, expressive lines in a modern harmonic language.
p0426.rw: Modern lyrical choice for expressive players

p0429.d: A theatrical violin and piano piece evoking a tightrope walker, with the pianist also playing inside the instrument; precarious, glassy textures and sudden outbursts.
p0429.rw: Striking and imaginative; needs a bold pianist

p0438.d: A Romantic violin showpiece: brilliant passagework, bold double stops and a sweet lyrical theme. A popular step towards the big concertos.

p0442.d: Haydn's bright early violin concerto with a confident, galant first movement and elegant figuration. Demands clean intonation and stylish Classical bowing.
p0442.rw: Elegant; less flashy than other options

p0447.d: Haydn's C major violin concerto complete: galant first movement, a serenade-like Adagio over pizzicato, and a lively Presto finale.
p0447.rw: Elegant but modest for this level

p0448.d: The finale of Haydn's C major violin concerto: a quick, cheerful Presto with running passagework and crisp bowing.
p0448.rw: Bright, fun finale; needs clean fingers

p0450.d: A violin arrangement of the Israeli national anthem's melody: a slow, plaintive minor-key tune, building in intensity.
p0450.rw: Simple tune; limited scope to impress

p0461.d: Hindemith's solo violin sonatas Op.31: compact, multi-movement works mixing neo-Baroque counterpoint, lyrical song and spiky energy (No.2 ends with Mozart-song variations).

p0468.d: Hindemith's early two-movement violin sonata in E flat (1918): a fresh, energetic opening and a slow, dance-like second movement. Post-Romantic yet already distinctly modern.

p0488.d: Ireland's wartime violin sonata, which made his name: impassioned outer movements around a hymn-like slow movement, warmly Romantic and expansive.

p0492.d: Janáček's only violin sonata: four short, restless movements full of nervous tremolos, folk-like fragments and sudden outbursts, written around the First World War.
p0492.rw: Intense and original; needs vivid characterisation

p0497.d: Opening movement of Kabalevsky's youthful violin concerto: bright, energetic and tuneful, with Soviet-style folk-like themes and brilliant passagework.

p0499.d: Opening movement of Kabalevsky's youthful violin concerto: bright, energetic and tuneful, with Soviet-style folk-like themes and brilliant passagework.

p0506.d: Khachaturian's early 'song-poem' in homage to Armenian folk singers: an improvisatory, rhapsodic piece with exotic modal colour and passionate climaxes.

p0507.d: Khachaturian's early 'song-poem' in homage to Armenian folk singers: an improvisatory, rhapsodic piece with exotic modal colour and passionate climaxes.

p0510.d: Opening movement of Khachaturian's violin concerto: driving, folk-dance energy, a sensuous second theme and a brilliant cadenza.

p0511.d: One of three romances by violinist-composer Roman Kim, presumably lyrical in character and written by a virtuoso with an ear for the instrument's possibilities.

p0514.d: An early, warmly Romantic slow piece by Kodály: a long, rising melody of broad expressive sweep.
p0514.rw: Beautiful lyric piece; good tone showcase

p0517.d: Unaccompanied violin piece: a free, rhetorical recitative followed by a quick, playful scherzo in Kreisler's Viennese manner, rich in double stops.

p0518.d: Kreisler's evocation of Chinese music: a dazzling, perpetual-motion encore with a sultry middle section.
p0518.rw: Sparkling encore; maybe light for this level

p0519.d: Kreisler's set of variations on a Corelli theme, written 'in the style of Tartini': a noble Baroque-flavoured theme followed by increasingly decorative variations.
p0519.rw: Elegant and accessible; shows style and tone

p0520.d: Kreisler's set of variations on a Corelli theme, written 'in the style of Tartini': a noble Baroque-flavoured theme followed by increasingly decorative variations.
p0520.rw: Elegant and accessible; shows style and tone

p0522.d: American violin showpiece imitating a banjo with pizzicato and a fiddler with hoedown bowing; lively and fun.

p0524.d: Slow movement of Lalo's Symphonie espagnole: a darkly expressive, Spanish-tinged song over a rich accompaniment.
p0524.rw: Gorgeous slow movement; rewards a big tone

p0528.d: Opening movement of the Symphonie espagnole: bold, rhetorical and full of Spanish rhythms, with fiery passagework and sweeping melody.

p0529.d: The Scherzando second movement of the Symphonie espagnole: a light, graceful Spanish-style dance with delicate bowing.

p0530.d: Two or more movements from Lalo's five-movement Spanish-flavoured violin work, combining fiery rhetoric, dance rhythms and lyrical song.

p0537.d: A set of variation-like 'metamorphoses' for violin and piano, in Leighton's intense, chromatic style, ranging from lyrical to aggressive.

p0549.d: First movement of Lutosławski's Partita: an energetic Allegro giusto with sharp rhythms and bright, angular writing.

p0550.d: Lutosławski's Partita for violin and piano: five movements with three main movements linked by aleatoric interludes where the players' parts are not coordinated.
p0550.rw: Major modern work; strong ensemble needed

p0551.d: Short, mercurial piece for violin and piano, written as a competition test piece: sudden changes of mood and tempo, with flashes of virtuosity.

p0552.d: A slow, meditative piece for violin and piano based on a Good Friday chant, mostly quiet and inward, with long sustained lines.

p0562.d: Martinů's second violin sonata: neoclassical energy and Czech-flavoured lyricism in three movements, with rhythmic drive throughout.

p0567.d: Famous contemplative intermezzo from Massenet's opera Thaïs, in Marsick's violin transcription: long, singing line in D with harp-like piano, training sustained tone, vibrato and expressive shifting.

p0572.d: The famous opening movement: a soaring, restless E minor melody, brilliant passagework and a written-out cadenza that flows straight into the recapitulation. Graceful but exposed.
p0572.rw: Core repertoire; superb music that shows real command

p0573.d: Either the dramatic first movement plus the song-like Andante, or the Andante with the light, sparkling scherzo-like finale. A complete-feeling pairing of one of the best-loved concertos.

p0574.d: The complete concerto, played without breaks: impassioned first movement, tender Andante and a featherlight, elfin finale. Needs elegance, clean spiccato and stamina rather than raw power.
p0574.rw: Audience favourite; complete and satisfying programme anchor

p0581.d: An early Messiaen piece for violin and piano: rhapsodic, by turns ecstatic and dancing, with rich modal harmony. Rediscovered only in 2007, it needs intense tone and rhythmic precision.
p0581.rw: Striking and rarely heard; impressive with a fine pianist

p0585.d: Written as a wedding gift to his wife: a solemn theme and five variations that grow from calm to blazing intensity, ending in an ecstatic slow apotheosis high on the E string.

p0595.d: Mompou's delicate piano miniature from Scènes d'enfants, heard here in a violin arrangement: a gentle, Catalan-flavoured melody with bell-like harmonies. Simple surface, needs refined tone and poise.

p0599.d: The famous gypsy-style showpiece: a mournful slow introduction then accelerating fast sections with flashy runs, harmonics and a sultry middle part. Instantly recognisable.

p0613.d: A spirited, sunny sonata-form Allegro where violin and piano are true partners. Clean, elegant playing and light bow strokes required.

p0615.d: A brilliant, high-spirited sonata-form opening where violin and piano trade themes. Requires light bow strokes, clean passagework and Classical poise.

p0621.d: A choice among Mozart's violin concertos 2-5, all elegant, operatic and stylistically exposed works with cadenzas. Nos. 3-5 are the most played.
p0621.rw: Core repertoire; reveals taste and polish

p0625.d: Sunny, spirited opening movement of the G major concerto, with quick passagework, operatic lyricism and a cadenza.

p0626.d: Festive, military-flavoured opening movement of the D major concerto: bright high-register lines, elegant passagework and a cadenza.

p0629.d: A grand slow introduction leading to an elegant, energetic Allegro; one of Mozart's most mature violin sonatas, with an equal partnership with the piano.

p0634.d: A complete mature Mozart violin sonata: K.454 is noble and expansive; K.526 brilliant, with a famously fast perpetual-motion finale. True duo partnerships.
p0634.rw: Major chamber works; strong pianist needed

p0635.d: A brilliant, high-spirited Allegro vivace with bright themes shared between violin and piano. Requires crisp, light bow strokes.

p0636.d: A cheerful, bright first movement with a lively equal dialogue between violin and piano. Clean and elegant.

p0641.d: A slow, songful movement from a modern French suite for solo violin: an introspective, chant-like melody with expressive double stops. Tonal and accessible.

p0648.d: One caprice from Paganini's legendary set of 24 unaccompanied studies, covering every virtuoso technique: ricochet, double stops, tenths, left-hand pizzicato and more.

p0652.d: A contemporary violin piece by Roxanna Panufnik, presumably inspired by Alice in Wonderland: likely whimsical and colourful. Details not well documented.

p0654.d: A set of unaccompanied variations written in homage to Penderecki (Luslawice is his home village). Modern idiom, exploring varied textures and techniques.

p0655.d: Penderecki's unaccompanied cadenza, adapted from his viola concerto: an intense, lamenting slow section framing a driving fast middle, with fierce double stops.

p0656.d: An intense unaccompanied work adapted from Penderecki's viola concerto: anguished slow writing around a relentless fast middle section, with heavy double stops.

p0677.d: Poulenc's wartime Violin Sonata, dedicated to the memory of Lorca: tense, angular outer movements frame a tender Intermezzo. Demanding ensemble and a darker side of Poulenc.
p0677.rw: Powerful but less often chosen than other French sonatas

p0678.d: A single-movement fantasy by Florence Price for violin and piano, mixing Romantic lyricism with spiritual- and folk-tinged melody. Warm and singing rather than showy.
p0678.rw: Fresh, rewarding repertoire with strong melodic appeal

p0680.d: Prokofiev's five short wordless songs for violin and piano, arranged from his vocalises. Delicate, lyrical miniatures with subtle harmonic colour and refined high-register writing.
p0680.rw: Exquisite miniatures; showcase tone and colour

p0681.d: First movement of Prokofiev's Second Violin Concerto: opens with an unaccompanied folk-like theme, then develops into lyrical and sardonic music. Classical in shape, demanding in control and tone.

p0682.d: Prokofiev's First Violin Concerto: dreamy, shimmering opening, a fiercely virtuosic scherzo and a luminous finale. Unconventional and colourful, with very exposed high writing.
p0682.rw: Brilliant, imaginative concerto; strong diploma choice

p0683.d: Prokofiev's Second Violin Concerto complete: a folk-like opening, a famously lyrical slow movement, and a rhythmic, castanet-flavoured finale. Balances lyricism and bite.

p0684.d: Three of Prokofiev's Five Melodies for violin and piano: short, wordless songs with soaring lines and subtle shifting harmonies. Requires a refined, varied tone more than fireworks.
p0684.rw: Exquisite miniatures; showcase tone and colour

p0687.d: First two movements of Prokofiev's Violin Sonata No. 2 (his own version of the Flute Sonata): a graceful, classical Moderato and a sparkling, energetic Scherzo.

p0688.d: Prokofiev's Sonata for solo violin (often played by a group of violinists in unison): classical in shape, bright and clear, with a theme-and-variations middle movement.
p0688.rw: Clean and attractive, though less dramatic than the concertos

p0695.d: Prokofiev's Violin Sonata No. 2, his own version of the Flute Sonata: graceful, sunny and classical in form, with a sparkling scherzo and a brilliant finale.

p0696.d: Pärt's meditative tintinnabuli piece (1977), arranged for many instruments: a chant-like sequence of variations separated by drone-like pauses. Hypnotic and atmospheric.
p0696.rw: Atmospheric and striking; a memorable recital item

p0710.d: Violin transcription of Ravel's Vocalise-étude en forme de habanera: a languid, sultry Spanish dance with sinuous chromatic melody and subtle rhythmic sway.
p0710.rw: Atmospheric and short; good colour contrast

p0711.d: One or two movements from Ravel's Violin Sonata No. 2: a cool, transparent Allegretto, a jazzy 'Blues', and a relentless perpetuum mobile finale. Highly polished writing.
p0711.rw: Iconic French sonata; flexible movement choice

p0712.d: Two movements from Ravel's Violin Sonata No. 2, including the jazz-inflected 'Blues' with either the delicate Allegretto or the breathless Perpetuum mobile finale.
p0712.rw: Iconic French sonata; stylish and distinctive

p0713.d: Ravel's Violin Sonata No. 2 complete: a translucent opening, the jazz-tinged 'Blues', and a dazzling Perpetuum mobile. Precise, colourful and rhythmically exacting.

p0714.d: Ravel's gypsy rhapsody: a long, fiery unaccompanied opening cadenza, then increasingly wild Hungarian-style dances. A real virtuoso showpiece full of harmonics, double stops and left-hand pizzicato.
p0714.rw: Spectacular showpiece; huge payoff if secure

p0715.d: Ravel's gypsy rhapsody: a long unaccompanied opening cadenza leads to increasingly wild Hungarian-style dances, packed with harmonics, double stops and left-hand pizzicato.
p0715.rw: Spectacular showpiece; huge payoff if secure

p0717.d: Reger's solo violin sonata Op. 42 no. 1: Bach-inspired structure with dense chordal writing, fugal textures and a chromatic late-Romantic voice.
p0717.rw: Substantial Bach-inspired work; less often heard

p0725.d: Violin arrangement of themes from Carlos Rafael Rivera's score for The Queen's Gambit: wistful, cinematic melody building in intensity.
p0725.rw: Popular TV music; appealing to younger players

p0727.d: First two movements of Rodrigo's 'Summer Concerto' for violin: a neo-Baroque, lively opening and a Siciliana slow movement with Spanish flavour.

p0728.d: An arrangement of the world's most famous tango: dramatic, rhythmic, with sultry melody and theatrical contrasts. Fun to play and well known to audiences.
p0728.rw: Crowd-pleaser; lighter weight at diploma level

p0730.d: Violin arrangement of the bluegrass fiddle classic, imitating a speeding train with whistles, slides and fast, driving bowing. Energetic and showy.

p0734.d: First and third movements of Rubbra's Second Violin Sonata: passionate English lyricism with modal colour, and a vigorous, dance-like finale.

p0739.d: Saariaho's short solo violin Nocturne, written in memory of Lutosławski: fragile, shadowy textures using harmonics, glissandi and microtonal shading.
p0739.rw: Atmospheric; suits players drawn to modern sound

p0740.d: Saariaho's Tocar ('to touch') for violin and piano: the two instruments gradually converge, with shimmering textures, extended techniques and subtle sound colour.

p0744.d: Two movements from Saint-Saëns's Third Violin Concerto: a dramatic first movement, a barcarolle-like Andantino and a fiery finale with a hymn-like chorale. Elegant and brilliant.

p0746.d: Saint-Saëns's Third Violin Concerto complete: dramatic, lyrical and brilliant, with a lilting slow movement and a finale climaxing in a hymn-like chorale.

p0748.d: First movement of Saint-Saëns's Third Violin Concerto: a bold, dramatic opening on the G string, contrasted with a sweet lyrical theme and brilliant passagework.

p0749.d: Violin and piano version of Saint-Saëns's spooky waltz of skeletons, with the detuned E string, dance rhythms and macabre wit.
p0749.rw: Vivid and fun; audiences love it

p0750.d: Saint-Saëns's Havanaise: a languid Cuban habanera rhythm with sensuous melody and brilliant flourishes, building to virtuosic passages. Requires charm and rhythmic poise.

p0751.d: Saint-Saëns's Havanaise: a languid habanera rhythm with sensuous melody and brilliant flourishes. Needs elegance, rhythmic poise and secure virtuosity.

p0752.d: Saint-Saëns's Introduction and Rondo capriccioso: a melancholy Spanish-tinged introduction, then a sparkling, capricious rondo with dazzling passagework.
p0752.rw: Classic violin showpiece; huge audience appeal

p0753.d: Saint-Saëns's Introduction and Rondo capriccioso (piano part as transcribed by Bizet): melancholy introduction, then a sparkling Spanish-flavoured rondo with dazzling passagework.
p0753.rw: Classic violin showpiece; huge audience appeal

p0754.d: Saint-Saëns's late Élégie for violin and piano: a short, poignant, intimate lament with expressive lines and restrained intensity.

p0755.d: Salonen's solo violin piece (the title means 'unlearned laughter'): an intense chaconne-like work building through driving rhythm, multiple stops and virtuosic figuration.

p0757.d: Sarasate's Carmen Fantasy: a dazzling medley of Bizet's tunes (Aragonaise, Habanera, Seguidilla, Gypsy Dance) with harmonics, left-hand pizzicato and breakneck passagework.

p0760.d: Sarasate's Zigeunerweisen: a dramatic gypsy-style lament followed by a fiery Hungarian czardas finale with harmonics and left-hand pizzicato.

p0761.d: Sarasate's Zigeunerweisen: a dramatic gypsy lament followed by a dazzling czardas with harmonics, left-hand pizzicato and rapid passagework.

p0762.d: Schoenberg's last instrumental work: a compact, twelve-tone fantasy for violin with piano, full of dramatic gestures, fragmented lyricism and sudden contrasts.
p0762.rw: Major modernist statement; demanding for listeners

p0766.d: Schubert's 'Grand Duo' violin sonata in A: genial, songful and classical in proportion, with a sparkling scherzo and lively finale.

p0768.d: Schubert's Rondo in A for violin and strings: a slow introduction followed by a genial, sunny rondo with lively passagework.
p0768.rw: Charming Schubert; fresh alternative to concertos

p0770.d: Last two movements of Schubert's Duo in A: a vigorous scherzo with a lyrical trio, and a bright, energetic finale.

p0775.d: Three short, linked character pieces moving from dreamy and tender to warm, then to a fiery, driving finale. Originally for clarinet; needs rich tone and sustained Romantic phrasing.
p0775.rw: Beloved Romantic set; showcases tone and musicianship

p0785.d: First two movements of Schumann's dark, passionate A minor sonata: a restless, impassioned opening and a gentle, wistful Allegretto. Dense textures demand a full tone.

p0786.d: Schumann's large-scale D minor sonata: a dramatic, densely argued first movement and a hushed, hymn-like slow movement with variations. Big in scale and emotionally intense.
p0786.rw: Powerful but heavy-going; less often chosen

p0787.d: Schumann's compact, stormy A minor sonata in three movements: passionate, wistful and then a driving moto perpetuo finale. Equal partnership with the piano.

p0790.d: A single-movement piece for violin and piano by Mátyás Seiber, mixing lyrical and rhythmically energetic writing in a mid-century modernist idiom.

p0794.d: The concerto's opening Nocturne: a long, brooding, slow meditation with muted orchestral textures. Demands sustained tone and intense control rather than speed.
p0794.rw: Profound music; needs great tonal stamina

p0797.d: A short piano prelude from Op.34 arranged for violin and piano, in Shostakovich's witty, bittersweet miniature style.
p0797.rw: Brief miniature; slight for a fellowship

p0801.d: The epic, rhapsodic first movement: hushed opening, soaring melodies, a central cadenza and blazing virtuosity. One of the hardest movements in the standard violin repertoire.

p0802.d: Complete concerto: brooding, rhapsodic first movement, a warm hymn-like Adagio and a heavy, dance-like finale full of double stops and harmonics.

p0804.d: A quiet, slow postlude for violin and piano in Silvestrov's 'post-modern' style: fragile echoes of Romantic gestures, hushed dynamics and suspended time.

p0806.d: A fiery virtuoso rhapsody for violin and piano drawing on Hutsul folk music from the Carpathians: improvisatory slow sections and wild, fast dance passages.

p0808.d: Two Bohemian duos for violin and piano: a warm, folk-flavoured song leading into lively dance music. Romantic and tuneful, with some virtuoso flourishes.

p0809.d: Ethel Smyth's large A minor sonata in Brahmsian Romantic style, full of passion and rich textures; the chosen pairs give either the first half or the second half.
p0809.rw: Rewarding rediscovery; less familiar to examiners

p0819.d: A short, muted, slow-moving elegy for solo violin (written for viola too), in quiet contrapuntal lines. Austere and inward rather than showy.
p0819.rw: Austere and short for a fellowship

p0820.d: A short, muted, slow-moving elegy for solo violin (written for viola too), in quiet contrapuntal lines. Austere and inward rather than showy.

p0826.d: Four contrasting character pieces: a passionate Quasi ballata, a fiery Appassionato, the tender Un poco triste and a virtuosic Burleska. Lush late-Romantic Czech writing.

p0828.d: Four contrasting character pieces: a passionate Quasi ballata, a fiery Appassionato, the tender Un poco triste and a virtuosic Burleska. Lush late-Romantic Czech writing.
p0828.rw: Lovely music; pair with Burleska for impact

p0833.d: A slow, elegiac piece from Trinity's 2025 Grade 8 violin book, as the title suggests; needs sustained, expressive tone.

p0835.d: An exotic, sensuous aria from the opera King Roger, transcribed by Kochański: languid, ornamented melody over rich harmonies, rising to ecstatic heights.

p0836.d: An exotic, sensuous aria from the opera King Roger, transcribed by Kochański: languid, ornamented melody over rich harmonies, rising to ecstatic heights.

p0837.d: The first and most famous of the Myths: glittering piano water-textures under a floating, ecstatic violin line full of colour and harmonics.

p0839.d: Szymanowski's impressionist tone-poems on Greek myths: shimmering, perfumed textures with harmonics, quarter-tone-like slides and rapturous climaxes. Technically and musically extreme.

p0840.d: A piece by Bulgarian-British composer Tabakova inspired by the Rhodope mountains, likely blending folk-like modal melody and drones with a contemporary sound.

p0846.d: A dreamy, floating piece for violin and piano with soft, shimmering harmonies, glissandi and free-flowing time. Evocative and delicate rather than virtuosic.

p0851.d: The famous 'Devil's Trill' sonata: a lilting siciliano, a lively Allegro and a dramatic finale crowned by the notorious trills with accompanying melody in double stops.

p0853.d: Opening movements of the 'Dido abandoned' sonata: an expressive, sorrowful Affettuoso and a vigorous, energetic Presto in Tartini's galant style.

p0854.d: The concerto's slow movement: a melancholy, song-like canzonetta in G minor with a warmer middle section, played muted. Needs a singing tone and natural phrasing.
p0854.rw: Gorgeous melody; perfect Grade 8 slow piece

p0855.d: Either the expansive, virtuosic first movement with its big cadenza, or the plaintive Canzonetta leading straight into the fiery Russian-dance finale.

p0856.d: Tchaikovsky's complete violin concerto: lyrical, expansive first movement with cadenza, a wistful Canzonetta and a whirling folk-dance finale. A pinnacle of Romantic virtuosity.

p0859.d: Three pieces: a soulful Méditation, an agile, scherzo-like Scherzo and a sweet, singing Mélodie. Varied and idiomatic, full of Tchaikovsky's melodic warmth.

p0870.d: A solo violin work by Augusta Read Thomas; expect a free, chant-like line with fluid rhythms and bright modern colours, demanding control of tone and pacing.
p0870.rw: Distinctive modern voice; suits imaginative players

p0873.d: An arrangement of the famous Russian gypsy romance: smoky, slow opening that accelerates into fiery, virtuoso variations full of rubato and flair.
p0873.rw: Audience favourite; huge fun to play

p0877.d: First movement of Turina's Sonata Española for violin and piano: Andalusian colour, sweeping melody, Spanish dance inflections and colourful, rich piano writing.

p0879.d: Ustvolskaya's austere, uncompromising violin sonata: stark, hammered textures, relentless rhythms and bleak intensity with little conventional lyricism.
p0879.rw: Striking and intense; needs a committed performer

p0883.d: A dramatic, operatic first movement with a passionate cadenza and big lyrical themes; the concerto's movements run on, so this is the substantial core.
p0883.rw: Classic diploma concerto; balanced lyricism and display

p0885.d: A grand Baroque chaconne in G minor (attribution to Vitali is doubtful): a set of increasingly dramatic variations over a repeated bass, full of pathos and display.
p0885.rw: Dramatic and well-loved; strong stamina test

p0886.d: The bright, famous opening of 'Spring': ritornello alternates with solo episodes depicting birdsong, streams and a storm, needing crisp, lively bowing.
p0886.rw: Instantly recognisable and fun; shows clean bowing

p0897.d: George Walker's first violin sonata: compact and concentrated, mixing angular modernist lines with lyrical, blues- and spiritual-tinged warmth.

p0899.d: Two contrasting Walton miniatures: a wistful, lilting Canzonetta and a quick, witty Scherzetto with playful rhythms and bright sparkle.
p0899.rw: Elegant pairing; good contrast and charm

p0901.d: First movement of Walton's concerto: dreamy, bittersweet lyricism over a restless accompaniment, with glittering, demanding passagework and wide expressive range.

p0903.d: Walton's violin sonata in two substantial movements: a warm, rhapsodic Allegro tranquillo and a set of variations ending in a vigorous coda.

p0904.d: Walton's violin sonata in two substantial movements: a warm, rhapsodic Allegro tranquillo and a set of variations ending in a vigorous coda.

p0905.d: Walton's Two Pieces for violin and piano (Canzonetta and Scherzetto): a wistful song and a light, quick-witted scherzo.
p0905.rw: Elegant pairing; good contrast and charm

p0914.d: A passionate, songful first movement with Romantic sweep and brilliant passagework; it leads directly into the famous Romance.

p0915.d: Wieniawski's complete second concerto: an ardent first movement, a tender Romance, and a fiery gypsy-style finale full of dazzling technique.

p0916.d: A romantic, story-like piece: a melancholy song framing a stormy, double-stop-laden middle section; intensely expressive.

p0917.d: A swaggering, elegant polonaise with a lyrical middle section, packed with brilliant passagework, double stops and bravura flourishes.

p0919.d: A proud, ceremonial polonaise with a singing central episode and dazzling virtuoso writing; a classic Romantic recital showpiece.

p0922.d: A breathless, fiery tarantella with relentless spiccato, ricochet and fast passagework, contrasted by a short lyrical middle section.

p0925.d: A violin piece evoking the legend of the bluebird; expect a lyrical, fairy-tale character with delicate, expressive writing.

p0926.d: The brisk, neo-Baroque first movement of Vaughan Williams's violin concerto: vigorous, modal and contrapuntal with busy string-crossing solo writing.
p0926.rw: Fine music, but less showy than alternatives

p0930.d: The finale of Vaughan Williams's late violin sonata: a set of variations on a grave theme, ranging from introspective to vigorous, ending quietly.
p0930.rw: Rewarding but austere; less often chosen

p0931.d: A rhapsody for violin and orchestra depicting a skylark's ascent: floating unaccompanied cadenzas, pastoral folk-like melodies and long, hushed high lines.
p0931.rw: Beloved masterpiece; exacting control of sound

p0934.d: An arrangement of the Jacobite Scottish song, likely presenting the tender melody then decorating it with variations and Scottish flourishes.

p0937.d: A dark, brooding elegy for violin and piano, the violin's G string tuned down; rich, passionate and harmonically lush, with a dramatic climax.
p0937.rw: Intense and beautiful; demands sustained tone

p0939.d: A single-movement 'Ballade' for solo violin: a recitative-like opening leading to a fierce, chordal Allegro in fiery rhythm; dense and dramatic.
p0939.rw: Iconic solo showpiece; concentrated and dramatic
