s0761.d: Arrangement of George Ezra's upbeat 2018 hit 'Shotgun'; catchy, bouncy melody with pop syncopation that young players instantly recognise.
s0761.rw: Catchy pop hit; motivating for kids

s0763.d: An arrangement of a gavotte from François Couperin's trio-sonata suite 'La Françoise' (Les Nations): an elegant French Baroque dance with lilting rhythm and graceful phrasing.
s0763.rw: Elegant Baroque dance at an easy level

s0765.d: The lively finale of Küchler's student concertino in D: bright, rhythmic first-position (with some third) writing in a Classical/Baroque pastiche, a classic pupil concerto.
s0765.rw: Classic student concertino; feels like a real concerto

s0766.d: The giga from Veracini's E minor 'academic' sonata: a vigorous Baroque jig with driving compound rhythm, string crossings and bold character.

s0768.d: Florence Price's 'Elf Dance' for violin and piano: light, fleet and playful, with quick figurations and delicate bowing evoking fairy-like dancers.

s0770.d: Florence Price's wistful violin-and-piano miniature (c.1933): a gently melancholy D minor melody with spiritual-like warmth, ideal for singing tone and expressive phrasing.

s0771.d: Arrangement of Ariana Grande's 2014 pop ballad 'One Last Time'; a catchy, emotive melody with pop syncopations, practising tone and rhythmic feel.
s0771.rw: Motivating pop choice; less musical depth

s0776.d: Gently flowing Andante for violin and piano, warm and songlike with Fauré's shifting harmonies; needs sustained bow control and subtle colour more than fireworks.
s0776.rw: Lovely but less known than Fauré's other violin pieces

s0778.d: Fauré's famous Berceuse (lullaby): a rocking piano accompaniment under a tender, arching violin melody that climbs higher as it grows; demands even bowing and smooth shifts.

s0782.d: A short lyrical piece by Fauré, originally for violin and piano; flowing and elegant, testing tone control and phrasing.

s0795.d: A spirited 'gypsy' dance in a Hungarian-flavoured style, with lively rhythms and contrasting sections; builds bow control and character (ending at bar 47).
s0795.rw: Lively character piece; good for confidence

s0796.d: A short new piece from the Trinity Grade 1 book, named after a north London square; simple melodic writing to practise steady bowing and rhythm.

s0797.d: A short new piece named after a Hackney park, from the Trinity Grade 2 book; likely a cheerful tune practising simple bowing patterns and rhythm.

s0798.d: A folk-style reel with leaping intervals, as the title suggests; quick, dancing fiddle writing that tests string crossings, agile bowing and clean leaps.
s0798.rw: Energetic fiddle style; fun to perform

s0799.d: A Latin-flavoured piece evoking Brazilian and Cuban dance styles; syncopated rhythms and bright character demand rhythmic precision and flair.

s0801.d: A simple Baroque air by Gottfried Finger, a graceful tune in a dance-like metre; practises even bowing, phrasing and clean intonation.

s0802.d: Arrangement of a gentle Baroque air by Finger with an optional trill; a graceful melody for learning phrasing and basic ornamentation.

s0803.d: The finale of Finzi's early violin concerto: a jaunty English hornpipe-style rondo, bright and rhythmic, with brisk passagework and pastoral lyrical moments.
s0803.rw: Fresh English concerto movement; rarely heard

s0805.d: Jazz ballad 'When Sunny Gets Blue' (Marvin Fisher, 1956) arranged for violin; a smoky, slow standard needing relaxed swing phrasing and expressive slides.
s0805.rw: Stylish jazz ballad; shows musical maturity

s0809.d: Arrangement of the haunting waltz 'Once Upon a December' from the film Anastasia: a wistful 3/4 melody. Practises smooth legato phrasing and flowing triple time.

s0810.d: Arrangement of Flanders & Swann's comic 'Hippopotamus Song' ('Mud, mud, glorious mud'); a jaunty, humorous tune practising steady rhythm and character.

s0818.d: Opening Allegro from a sonata by Edinburgh composer David Foulis, in Italianate Baroque style; bright E major passagework that tests string crossing and clean fingerwork.

s0820.d: Slow movement from Seitz's G major student concerto: a simple, songful Adagio that develops tone, sustained bowing and expressive phrasing.

s0825.d: Arrangement of the well-known Gavotte attributed to Padre Martini; a poised, cheerful Baroque dance with neat rhythms that practises crisp bowing and lightness.

s0827.d: Duet arrangement of a gentle pastoral melody by singing teacher Giuseppe Concone; a flowing, lyrical tune that practises legato and ensemble listening.

s0830.d: Violin arrangement of Porgy's carefree banjo song from Porgy and Bess; bouncy and syncopated, practising rhythm and cheerful character.

s0832.d: Heifetz's brilliant transcription of Sportin' Life's sly song from Porgy and Bess; bluesy slides, double stops and virtuoso flourishes demand flair and swagger.

s0836.d: Violin melody of the classic tango 'La cumparsita'; dramatic, accented dance rhythms and a passionate tune practise rhythmic bite and style.

s0845.d: Birtel's violin arrangement of Gardel's famous tango 'Por una cabeza' (heard in Scent of a Woman); sultry, dramatic tango with expressive slides and rhythmic bite.

s0848.d: Arrangement of Erroll Garner's jazz ballad 'Misty'; a dreamy, slow standard demanding relaxed rhythm, smooth slides and expressive tone.

s0852.d: Klezmer arrangement of Mordechai Gebirtig's Yiddish song about Avreml the pickpocket; minor-mode melody with expressive ornaments and bittersweet character.

s0853.d: Klezmer arrangement of Gebirtig's Yiddish song 'Moishele my friend'; a wistful minor melody with klezmer ornaments, practising expressive tone.

s0855.d: Expressive Affettuoso and lively Allegro from Geminiani's C major violin sonata; Corelli-style Baroque writing with ornamentation, double stops and agile passagework.

s0857.d: Duet arrangement of the tango 'Flor de fango' by Augusto Gentile; a dramatic, rhythmic tango practising accents and ensemble playing.

s0870.d: Glazunov's Méditation: a warm, lyrical violin piece with a long, singing melody rising to an expressive climax; tests sustained tone and high positions.

s0871.d: Kreisler's violin arrangement of Glazunov's Spanish serenade; a lively, guitar-like Spanish-flavoured piece with pizzicato and rhythmic flair.

s0884.d: A gentle 'evening song' in salon style from the Trinity book: a lyrical melody calling for warm tone and shaped phrasing.
s0884.rw: Pleasant lyrical choice for tone work

s0885.d: A short, bright duet overture for Initial-grade violin, played with teacher; practises steady pulse and ensemble.

s0896.d: Arrangement of Chiquinha Gonzaga's Brazilian polka 'Atraente' (Attractive): a sparkling, syncopated salon dance with choro flavour.
s0896.rw: Charming Brazilian flavour; lively and fresh

s0902.d: A bright, drone-like rustic Tambourin attributed to Gossec, arranged for violin: fast, light bowing with a festive, folk-dance character.
s0902.rw: Energetic and fun; light bow work

s0906.d: Initial-grade arrangement of a Puerto Rican dance tune, 'The Puerto Rican Woman': simple, rhythmically lively Latin flavour.

s0911.d: Kreisler's arrangement of Grainger's Irish reel 'Molly on the Shore': a fast, sparkling fiddle tune with double stops and brisk, light bowing.

s0919.d: 'The Joker' from Grechaninov's 'Early Morning': a cheeky, playful miniature with crisp articulation and humorous contrasts.

s0932.d: A short Baroque-style 'Sinfonia' from Vamoosh Cello Book 1.5, practising steady pulse and smooth bowing.

s0933.d: A cool, laid-back jazzy piece from Vamoosh Bass Book 2: smooth swung rhythms suit the bass well.

s0935.d: A bright, rustic Tambourin by Grétry (via Suzuki Book 8): quick, drone-like dance with crisp, light bowing.

s0944.d: Arrangement of Solveig's Song from Peer Gynt: a wistful, folk-like minor melody alternating with a gentle lilting refrain.

s0955.d: Arrangement of Parashkev Hadjiev's Rondino: a bright, rhythmically lively Bulgarian-flavoured piece with playful recurring theme.

s0956.d: Arrangement of Parashkev Hadjiev's Rondino: a bright, rhythmically lively Bulgarian-flavoured piece with playful recurring theme.

s0964.d: The Allegro from Handel's E major violin sonata (HWV 373): a bright, energetic movement with running passagework and clear Baroque phrasing.

x00889.d: Brahms's brisk, stormy Scherzo from the joint FAE Sonata, with powerful chords and rhythmic drive. Tests strong bow control and energy.

x00890.d: Baroque sonata in C minor with expressive slow movements and brisk allegros. Practises ornament, double stops and style.

x00891.d: Kreutzer études for violin, the first working in double stops and chords and the other a dramatic caprice. Builds technical control.

x00892.d: Romantic first movement from Schumann's late A minor violin sonata, with a brooding opening and urgent, passionate main section. Needs stamina and drive.

x00893.d: Lyrical arrangement of a Russian maiden's song from Stravinsky's opera Mavra, simple in character with folk-like charm. Practises tone and phrasing.

x00894.d: Two movements from Stravinsky's suite drawn from Pulcinella, based on Pergolesi, witty and neoclassical. Practises rhythm, wit and double stops.

x00895.d: Unaccompanied Baroque fantasia with alternating slow and fast sections. Practises implied harmony, double stops and style.
x00895.rw: Authentic Baroque solo; flexible and popular

x01933.d: Opening movement of Bartók's second violin concerto, with a folk-tinged, rhythmic and virtuosic character; demands stamina and expressive power.

x01934.d: Tonia Ko's Plush Earth in Four Pieces, a contemporary violin work with delicate textures and extended techniques; practises colour and sound control.

x01935.d: Elena Langer's Transformations, a contemporary violin work blending lyricism and rhythm; practises expressive playing and flexibility.

x01936.d: Mozart's second violin concerto, two movements: elegant, lively Classical writing with cadenza; practises refined tone and phrasing.

x01937.d: Sarasate's Romanza Andaluza, a Spanish dance-like piece with lyrical melodies and brilliant passagework; practises expressive tone and flair.

x02891.d: Reflective contemporary violin piece by Alberga; lullaby-like with expressive intensity and modern colours.

x02892.d: Perlman arrangement of Joplin's ragtime piece; syncopated, charming and rhythmic.

x02893.d: Perlman's arrangement of Joplin's Easy Winners; bright, syncopated ragtime with double stops.

x02894.d: Elena Langer's lyrical piece with Russian-tinged harmony; a romantic love song for violin.

x02895.d: Atmospheric contemporary violin piece by Langer evoking a snowy landscape; textural effects and lyricism.

x02896.d: Mozart's mature E flat sonata, the first two movements; elegant, with clear phrasing and tonal polish.

x02897.d: Tartini's famous violin sonata with the Devil's Trill; double-trills and virtuosic cadenza.

x05638.d: British violin sonata with intense, rhapsodic writing and rhythmic energy; late-Romantic in manner.

x05639.d: Stravinsky's neoclassical suite from Pulcinella, arranged by Dushkin for violin: Introduzione, Serenata, Tarantella, etc.

x05640.d: Heifetz arrangement of Gershwin's lullaby and blues from Porgy and Bess; sultry and virtuosic.

x05641.d: Heifetz's arrangement of Gershwin's lament; dramatic, soulful and rhythmic.

y00187.d: Bach's Sonata in E minor, BWV 1023, for violin and continuo: a toccata-like opening, expressive Adagio ma non tanto, an Allemande and a Gigue, practising Baroque style.

y00188.d: First movement of Beethoven's Sonata in E♭, Op. 12 No. 3: a brilliant Allegro con spirito practising rhythmic energy, clean passagework and ensemble.

y00189.d: Dvořák's Four Romantic Pieces, Op. 75: short, melodic movements ranging from gentle to spirited, practising lyrical tone, double stops and Slavonic rhythm.

y00190.d: Fauré's Romance in B♭: a graceful, flowing romance practising singing tone, controlled vibrato and legato bowing.

y00191.d: Hindemith's Sonata in E♭, Op.11 No.1: an early, intense, expressive work in a late-Romantic idiom, practising rhythmic energy, tone and ensemble.

y00192.d: Leclair's Sonata in D, Op. 9 No. 3, ending with the famous 'Tambourin': Baroque dances and ornaments practising bow control, double stops and character.

y00193.d: First movement of Mozart's Sonata in B♭, K. 378: an Allegro moderato with the piano as equal partner, practising Classical phrasing, clarity and ensemble.

y00302.d: Lera Auerbach's T'filah (Prayer), Op. 33, for violin. Contemporary, meditative and intense, with expressive writing.

y00303.d: Adagio and Fuga from Bach's Solo Sonata No. 1 in G minor: a noble, chordal Adagio and a taxing four-voice Fugue training polyphony and chords.

y00304.d: First movement of Beethoven's Violin Concerto (1806), with its famous drum motif. Grand and lyrical, with cadenza and heavy technical demands.

y00305.d: First movement of Brahms's Violin Concerto (1878). Broad, symphonic scale and demanding double stops and runs.

y00306.d: Two movements of Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 1 (1773). An early, bright classical concerto; clean runs and elegant phrasing.

y00307.d: Two movements of Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 3 (1775). Graceful, singing concerto with clear Classical style and agility.

y00308.d: Two movements of Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 4 (1775). Bright with a brilliant rondo; trains clarity, articulation and style.

y00309.d: Two movements of Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 5, 'Turkish' (1775). Delightful, with a poignant Adagio and witty Rondo.

y00310.d: Sarasate's Spanish Dance Op. 21 No. 1 (c.1878), a lively Malagueña with flamenco character. Virtuoso double stops and harmonics.

y00311.d: Sarasate's Spanish Dance Op. 23 No. 6, a brilliant Zapateado in 3/4 and 6/8 rhythms. Fast, brilliant fingerwork and bow control.

y00312.d: Bernard Stevens's Sonata in A minor for violin, in one movement. Dramatic 20th-century language with intense lyrical sections.

y00467.d: Beethoven's Violin Sonata in E♭, Op. 12 No. 3 (1798). Grand and brilliant with a lyrical Adagio.

y00468.d: Beethoven's Violin Sonata in A minor, Op. 23 (1801). Terse and stormy with a playful Andante.

y00469.d: Beethoven's 'Spring' Sonata in F, Op. 24 (1801). Flowing and lyrical, with a lively Scherzo.

y00470.d: Beethoven's Violin Sonata in A, Op. 30 No. 1 (1802). Gentle, graceful with a variation finale.

y00471.d: Beethoven's Violin Sonata in C minor, Op. 30 No. 2 (1802). Dramatic and powerful, with a fiery finale.

y00472.d: Beethoven's Violin Sonata in G, Op. 30 No. 3 (1802). Sunny and witty with energetic runs.

y00473.d: Two movements of Brahms's Violin Sonata in G, Op. 78 'Rain' (1879). Warm, lyrical with a melancholy slow movement.

y00474.d: Two movements of Brahms's Violin Sonata in A, Op. 100 (1886). Sunny, flowing and lyrical.

y00475.d: First movement of Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 5 in A, K. 219 (1775). Elegant with surprising Adagio interruption.

y00476.d: First two movements of Mozart's Violin Sonata in B♭, K. 454 (1784). Dialogue between violin and piano in a refined Classical style.

y00477.d: Ysaÿe's Sonata No. 2 in A minor, Op. 27 (1923), dedicated to Jacques Thibaud. It quotes Bach and the Dies Irae; virtuoso unaccompanied writing.
y00477.rw: Celebrated and highly virtuosic solo work

y00761.d: Two of Sarasate's Spanish Dances: Malagueña, Romanza Andaluza or Zapateado, each a brilliant, dance-rhythmed showpiece with double stops, harmonics and fast passagework. Demands flair and secure intonation.

y00762.d: Up to two of Paganini's 24 Caprices for unaccompanied violin: concentrated studies in double stops, octaves, leaps, left-hand pizzicato and fast bowing. Intensely demanding.

y00763.d: Two of Szymanowski's Three Myths (Arethusa, Narcissus, Dryads and Pan): richly coloured, impressionistic pieces with harmonics, quarter-tone-like glissandi and virtuoso writing.

z00000.d: Dignified Baroque aria in D minor with a first variation of running semiquavers; trains smooth bowing, even tone and light ornamental decoration.
z00000.rw: Pleasant Baroque Nelson arrangement, modest challenge

z00001.d: Brisk binary Allegro in G with steady quaver and semiquaver passagework and sequences; practises clean detache, crisp string crossings and phrasing in Baroque style.
z00001.rw: Reliable Telemann, rewarding and not too hard

z00002.d: Slow, lyrical middle movement of a student concertino in G; sustained cantabile melody over a gentle accompaniment, practising vibrato, shifting and expressive phrasing.
z00002.rw: Sweet melody but overshadowed by outer movements

z00003.d: Slow Adagio followed by a quick Allegro assai from a Telemann sonatina in A: expressive ornamented line, then lively passagework and agile bowing.
z00003.rw: Attractive Telemann pairing, accessible at Grade 6

z00004.d: Fast unaccompanied movement in B minor, with a single line implying harmony and rapid figuration; trains clarity of bow strokes, string crossing and rhythmic drive without piano.
z00004.rw: Good solo Baroque showpiece, exposed throughout

z00005.d: Unaccompanied Fantasia pairing a slow Grave with a quick Allegro; practises double-stopped chords, stylish Baroque phrasing and independent musical judgement.
z00005.rw: Fine solo Telemann, demands good bow control

z00006.d: Warm, songlike Romance from Wieniawski's second concerto, with a sustained melody on the violin; trains rich tone, vibrato, shifting in higher positions and romantic rubato.
z00006.rw: Gorgeous Romantic melody that students love

z00007.d: Energetic opening of Bach's A minor concerto with driving rhythmic ritornello and episodes; practises stamina, clear articulation, string crossing and precise Baroque style.
z00007.rw: Core Baroque concerto, exam classic and rewarding

z00008.d: Spirited finale in A, marked Tempo giusto, with lively passagework and playful rhythms in the Classical style; practises agile bowing, crisp articulation and stamina.
z00008.rw: Solid Classical sonata finale, less well known

z00009.d: Brooding, wistful Un poco triste with a long arching melody over rich harmonies; practises expressive vibrato, dynamic shaping and Late Romantic rubato.
z00009.rw: Atmospheric Czech miniature, rewarding for musical students

z00423.d: Arrangement of the Air from Bach's Orchestral Suite no. 3, a serene, flowing melody. Practises long, even bows, smooth tone and sustained phrasing.

z00437.d: Slow, yearning piece by Amy Beach, with a rich melody and warm harmony. Practises sustained tone, expressive vibrato and smooth bow control.

z00438.d: Grave opening of Corelli's D major sonata in its original version, with stately chords and expressive lines. Practises double stops, grave Baroque style and ornamentation.

z00439.d: Graceful Menuetto and Trio from Schubert's A minor sonatina. Practises light dance character, clear bowing and contrast between minor and major sections.

z00440.d: Fast, bouncing Gigue from Bach's E major partita, played unaccompanied. Practises clean fast notes, string crossing and lively dance rhythm.

z00441.d: Theme and variations from the finale of Beethoven's A major violin sonata (op. 30 no. 1), light and varied. Practises contrasting character, ensemble with piano and clear articulation.

z00442.d: Final Rondo of Mozart's B flat violin sonata, cheerful and sparkling. Practises light spiccato, quick passagework and Classical clarity and wit.

z00443.d: Mazurka from Amy Beach's Three Compositions for violin, a spirited Polish dance. Practises mazurka rhythm, double stops and expressive rubato.

z00444.d: Fast Giga from Bach's D minor partita, played unaccompanied, with rapid 12/8 figures and double stops. Practises stamina, string crossing and lively dance rhythm.

z00445.d: Romanze, the slow movement of Wieniawski's Second Violin Concerto, a sweet, lyrical song. Practises expressive tone, high-position playing and vibrato.

Howard, arr. Gill: American songwriter best known for Fly Me to the Moon.

Kroll: American violinist, chamber musician and teacher who wrote popular violin pieces.
L. Cohen: Canadian singer-songwriter and poet, writer of Hallelujah.
de Falla: Foremost Spanish composer of his era, blending Andalusian folk music with modern French influences.
Menken, arr. Wyatt: American composer of Disney film musicals including The Little Mermaid, Aladdin and Pocahontas.
Judith Bell: Teacher-composer of pieces for young violinists.
Lagye: Belgian composer of salon pieces for violin and piano.
Iles: British jazz pianist, composer and educator.
Bach, J S, arr. Suzuki: German Baroque composer and organist, master of counterpoint; his suites, sonatas and partitas are core string repertoire.
N. Sokolovsky: Composer of short concert pieces for young violinists; details not confirmed.
Barbara Arens: Educational composer and arranger known for collections of pieces for young string players.
Barthélemon: French violinist and composer who worked mainly in London.
Beethoven: Towering composer who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras, transforming the symphony, sonata and string quartet.
Chen Yi: Chinese-American composer blending Chinese folk traditions with Western concert music.
Falk, Guetta, Kotecha, Tuinfort & Yacoub: Carl Falk, David Guetta, Savan Kotecha, Giorgio Tuinfort & Rami Yacoub
Pop songwriters and producers who co-wrote Ariana Grande's 2014 single 'One Last Time'.
Jean Baptiste Loeillet: Baroque composer from Ghent who published recorder and flute sonatas in Amsterdam.
Nancy Litten: Composer and string teacher who writes educational pieces for young players.
Chevalier de Saint-Georges: Guadeloupe-born violinist, fencer and composer; a leading Parisian musician of his day.
S. Nelson: Influential British string teacher and author of widely used beginner methods such as Essential String Method.
Bach, J S, arr. Mohrs: German Baroque composer and organist, master of counterpoint; his suites, sonatas and partitas are core string repertoire.
Sancho: Formerly enslaved writer and composer in Georgian London, the first known Black British composer to publish music.
Sarasate: Spanish violin virtuoso who wrote dazzling showpieces like Zigeunerweisen.
Sofia Gubaidulina: Tatar-Russian composer of spiritually charged, sonically adventurous music.
Janáček: Czech composer whose music draws on Moravian folk speech and song; known for operas like Jenůfa.
Flaherty, arr. Walshaw: American composer of musicals and film songs.
Sitt: Violinist, violist and teacher at Leipzig, prolific writer of studies and pieces for students.
Kraemer & Kraemer: Composer duo featured in Trinity's 2025 violin exam pieces.
F. Couperin: Leading French Baroque composer and harpsichordist, known as 'le Grand', famous for his harpsichord ordres and chamber music.
Pergolesi: Neapolitan composer of the Stabat Mater and La serva padrona; many works are falsely attributed to him.
Reena Esmail: Indian-American composer whose music draws together Hindustani and Western classical traditions.
Bruch: German Romantic composer famed for his violin concertos and Kol Nidrei.
Albéniz: Spanish pianist-composer whose colourful piano music, such as Iberia, drew on Andalusian folk idioms.
Ferraretto: Contemporary composer of new pieces for Trinity violin exam books.
Messiaen: Organist and composer whose music draws on birdsong, Catholic faith and unusual rhythms and modes.
Bach, J S: Leipzig cantor and towering Baroque master of counterpoint, keyboard, choral and instrumental music.
Schoenberg: Austrian-American composer who developed twelve-tone technique.
T. Anderson: Shetland fiddler, collector and teacher who preserved and composed many Shetland fiddle tunes.
Reger: German composer and organist, devoted to Bach-style counterpoint in a rich late-Romantic idiom.
Strauss, arr. Huws Jones: Viennese composer of waltzes and polkas, brother of Johann Strauss II.
Hille: Violinist and composer of salon and teaching pieces for violin.
Ellington & Strayhorn, arr. Garrick: Ellington, the great jazz bandleader, and Strayhorn, his long-time collaborator, co-wrote standards such as 'Satin Doll'.
Vivaldi: Venetian Baroque composer and violinist who wrote hundreds of concertos, including The Four Seasons.
Hess: Composer for film, TV and theatre, known for Ladies in Lavender and Hetty Wainthropp Investigates.
Ewa Iwan: Polish composer and teacher, author of the Musical Journeys series of imaginative pieces for young violinists.
Weinberger, arr. Arnell & Rokos: Composer whose folk-tinged opera Schwanda the Bagpiper was an international hit.
Mozart, arr. Wade: Prodigy and master of the Classical style; composed operas, symphonies, concertos and chamber music of extraordinary grace.
Tartini: Italian Baroque violinist, composer and theorist, famous for the Devil's Trill sonata.
Bonporti: Italian priest and composer whose violin Inventions were once mistaken for works by Bach.
Tacchinardi: Italian composer and teacher in Florence, known for short salon pieces for violin and piano.
Smart: Composer of a piece in Trinity's 2025 Grade 8 violin book; further details unknown.
Trory: Composer of educational violin pieces published in Trinity exam books.
Thomas Gregory: Violinist and educator, creator of the Vamoosh string books.
Ross Carey: Composer contributing to New Zealand educational string collections.
